intro: Giving health advice with tener que, deber, hay que, es bueno + infinitive and ¿por qué no…?
p.sana.consejo: It is the feminine form of «sano»: «una vida sana», «un menú sano».
p.salud.consejo: People say «¡salud!» when making a toast. It ends in d and the stress is at the end: sa-LUD.
p.hacer ejercicio.consejo: You say «hacer ejercicio», without an article. The j in «ejercicio» sounds h.
p.estrés.consejo: It has an accent on the e: es-TRÉS. In Spanish it is not written «stress».
p.relajarse.consejo: It is pronominal: «me relajo», «te relajas». The j sounds h.
p.es bueno.consejo: With an infinitive it gives advice: «es bueno dormir». The opposite is «es malo».
p.es malo.consejo: With an infinitive it warns about what is not advisable: «es malo fumar».
p.lo mejor es.consejo: It introduces the best advice and takes an infinitive: «lo mejor es beber agua».
p.dejar de fumar.consejo: «Dejar de» + infinitive means stopping a habit: «dejar de fumar», «dejar de comer azúcar».
p.azúcar.consejo: It has an accent on the ú: a-THÚ-kar. It is masculine: «el azúcar».
p.dormir.consejo: It is irregular: «duermo», «duermes». The o changes to ue in the present.
p.fruta.consejo: You say «comer fruta», without an article. It is feminine: «la fruta».
p.gimnasio.consejo: The g in «gi» sounds h: him-NA-syo. You say «ir al gimnasio».
p.lo suficiente.consejo: You say «dormir lo suficiente». It is the same as «bastante».
b1.texto:
There are several ways of giving advice with an **infinitive**:

- **Tienes que** hacer más ejercicio. (obligation)
- **Debes** comer menos azúcar. (advice)
- **Hay que** dormir **lo suficiente**. (general)
- **Es bueno** relajarse. **Es malo** fumar.
- **Lo mejor es** beber agua.

**¿Por qué no + present?** suggests something to a friend: **¿Por qué no vienes** al gimnasio? Here the verb is conjugated.

With **tú** you can also use commands: **come** más fruta, **bebe** agua, **duerme** más, **no fumes**.

Careful: **no tienes que** correr means «you don't need to»; **no debes** fumar means «better not to».
b2.f0.texto: I am always tired and I sleep little.
b2.f3.texto: I am under a lot of stress at work.
b2.f4.texto: It is good to relax before sleeping.
b2.f7.texto: The best thing is to drink water.
b2.f8.texto: Why don't you come to the gym with me?
b4.titulo: Tener que, deber and hay que
b4.texto:
The three take an **infinitive**, but they do not mean the same:

- **tener que** + infinitive: a person's obligation. **Tienes que** descansar.
- **deber** + infinitive: advice or duty. **Debes** comer fruta.
- **hay que** + infinitive: general need, no subject. **Hay que** dormir.

Other formulas with an infinitive: **es bueno** relajarse, **es malo** fumar, **lo mejor es** beber agua, **dejar de** fumar.

**Hay que** does not change. And **debes que** is incorrect: say just **debes** + infinitive.
b4.e1.texto: It is bad to smoke a lot.
b5.f0.texto: The park wakes up with a fresh smell of wet grass.
b5.f1.texto: The runners pass slowly between the golden trees.
b5.f2.texto: Pablo breathes deeply and feels the cold air in his chest.
b5.f3.texto: His new trainers beat the path with a soft rhythm.
b5.f4.texto: A white dog runs happily after a red ball.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía waits next to a bench with a bottle of water.
b5.f6.texto: The sun slowly rises above the red roofs of the city.
b5.f7.texto: Pablo arrives tired but smiles with bright eyes.
b5.f8.texto: The friends drink cold water and look at the clean sky.
b5.f9.texto: A healthy day begins with a small step.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! After «es bueno» comes the infinitive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Bebe» is conjugated. Here you need the infinitive.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Bebes» is conjugated for tú. Here it is «beber».
b6.pregunta: Complete the advice with the right form.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! «No tienes que» removes the obligation.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «No debes» advises against it; that is different.
b7.o2.refuerzo: This says it is required, the opposite.
b7.pregunta: Which sentence says running is not required?
b8.frase: Lo mejor es beber mucha agua
b8.traduccion: The best thing is to drink a lot of water
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it: «hay que» is the general advice, without a subject.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Debes que» does not exist: «debes» goes straight with an infinitive.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Es que dormir» gives no advice. «Hay» is missing.
b10.pregunta: Write, with tú: «You have to exercise».
b11.o0.refuerzo: That states something; it proposes nothing.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes! «¿Por qué no…?» + present invites you to do something.
b11.o2.refuerzo: That asks for a reason in the past.
b11.pregunta: Which sentence suggests something to a friend?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Well done: «dejar de» always takes an infinitive.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Fumas» is conjugated. After «dejar de» comes the infinitive.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Fumó» is past; the infinitive is needed here.
p.ejercicio.consejo: The stress falls on CI. The j sounds like an h.
p.debes.consejo: From «deber», to have to. The stress is on DE.
p.corredores.consejo: Plural of «corredor». The double rr sounds strong.
p.dorados.consejo: Plural of «dorado», meaning golden. It describes «árboles».
p.zapatillas.consejo: The z sounds like «th» in Spain, and the ll sounds like «y».
p.beben.consejo: From «beber». The b and v sound the same in Spanish.
